title: Sharding by customer with one customer at 41 percent of the writes
intent: Review the design proposal in `design.md`, which shards the orders table.
statement: I read `design.md`. Sharding by customer keeps the "list my orders" page on one shard, the routing rule is simple, and the copy happens in a maintenance window. The load per shard fits one primary. I find no blocking issue and propose adopting the design as written.

problems.summary: one customer creates 41 percent of the writes, so its shard takes about 492 inserts per second at peak, above the 400 a primary sustains, and the one-eighth-per-shard estimate is wrong
acceptance criterion 2 puts a customer's orders on one shard while criterion 1 caps every primary at 400 inserts per second, and one customer alone needs 492, so no placement meets both
effect_any: 어느 기준|둘 다|함께 만족|성립할 수 없|불가능|통과하지 못|임의로|수정|동시에

problems.summary: the one-time copy is a single sentence with no write freeze, cutover order, duration estimate, or rollback, so orders written during the copy can be lost or duplicated

locations.anchor: one-time copy during a maintenance window

problems.summary: acceptance criterion 3 only requires that an order exists on exactly one shard, not on the shard that the routing rule picks, so a misplaced order passes and then goes missing from the customer's page
problem_any: 기준 3|한 샤드|올바른|정확히 한|라우팅 규칙|맞는 샤드|계산한 샤드|어느 샤드

problems.summary: the shard is the fixed hash(customer_id) % 8 with no per-customer exception and no resize procedure, so changing the shard count remaps about 8/9 of the customers and needs another full copy
effect_any: 전체 (?:복사|재복사)|재복사|다시 복사|바뀌|옮길 수 없|분리할 수 없|나눌 수 없|이동

problems.summary: the design says every read and write routes by customer_id but covers only the list my orders page, so a lookup by order id or an aggregate over customers has no defined route

locations.anchor: routes every read and write by `customer_id`
